facts: The three angles of any triangle add to $180^{\circ}$, and the four angles of any quadrilateral add to $360^{\circ}$.
The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, and every angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$.
Opposite sides and opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, and all four sides of a rhombus or square are equal.
Every angle of a rectangle or square is $90^{\circ}$, and the angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal.
The diagonals of a parallelogram, rhombus, rectangle and square bisect each other, and those of a rectangle or square are also equal.
The diagonals of a rhombus or square bisect the vertex angles, and the axis of a kite bisects the other diagonal at right angles.
Angles on a straight line add to $180^{\circ}$, angles at a point add to $360^{\circ}$, and vertically opposite angles are equal.
On parallel lines, alternate and corresponding angles are equal, and co-interior angles add to $180^{\circ}$.
**Write a reason after every line**, as in $\angle ABD=24^{\circ}$ (angle sum of a triangle); a value with no reason is not a finished answer.
A property also works **backwards, as a test**: two equal angles make a triangle isosceles, and two pairs of equal opposite angles make a parallelogram.
steps: Mark on the figure every angle and length you already know.

Choose a relationship that helps find an unknown: an angle sum in a triangle or quadrilateral, angles on a straight line or at a point, parallel-line angles, equal sides or angles, or diagonal properties. Write an equation if needed, simplify it and solve for the unknown, giving a reason.
Repeat with each new value until you reach the unknown you were asked for.

b. $QR=PQ=5.5\text{ cm}$ (all sides of a rhombus are equal).

$PQ=QR$, so $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.

$\begin{aligned}\angle QPR=\angle PRQ&=(180^\circ-74^\circ)\div2\\&=53^\circ\end{aligned}$

a. Adjacent angles are co-interior on parallel sides and add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}(4x+6)+(2x+12)&=180\\6x+18&=180\\6x&=162\\x&=27\end{aligned}$

$\angle DAB=4(27)+6=114^\circ$.

$\angle BCD=114^\circ$ (opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal).

b. The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}70+105+(4t+5)+(3t+5)&=360\\7t+185&=360\\7t&=175\\t&=25\end{aligned}$

$\angle QRS=4(25)+5=105^\circ$ and $\angle RSP=3(25)+5=80^\circ$.

$\angle SPQ+\angle PQR=70^\circ+105^\circ=175^\circ$, so $PS$ and $QR$ are not parallel (co-interior angles on transversal $PQ$ do not add to $180^\circ$).

Therefore $PQRS$ is not a parallelogram.

a. Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.

$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB&=\frac{180^\circ-4t^\circ}{2}\\&=(90-2t)^\circ\end{aligned}$

Angles on the straight line $BCD$ add to $180^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}\angle ACD&=180^\circ-(90-2t)^\circ\\&=(90+2t)^\circ\end{aligned}$

b. $\angle MKN=v^\circ$ (base angles of $\triangle KMN$, since $KM=MN$).

$\angle KMN=(180-2v)^\circ$ (angle sum of $\triangle KMN$).

$\angle KML=180^\circ-(180-2v)^\circ=2v^\circ$ (angles on the straight line $LMN$).

$\angle LKM=2v^\circ$ (base angles of $\triangle KLM$, since $KL=LM$).

$\begin{aligned}u+2v+2v&=180\\u+4v&=180\end{aligned}$

The angles of $\triangle KLM$ add to $180^\circ$.

Let the interior angles be $p^\circ$, $q^\circ$ and $h^\circ$.

$r+p=360$, $s+q=360$ and $t+h=360$ (angles at a point).

Adding gives $r+s+t+p+q+h=1080$.

$p+q+h=180$ (angle sum of a triangle).

$\begin{aligned}r+s+t&=1080-180\\&=900\end{aligned}$

Every triangle has interior angle sum $180^\circ$, so the result is always $900$.

The angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal.

$\begin{aligned}3z+6&=5z-50\\2z&=56\\z&=28\end{aligned}$

$\angle KLM=\angle KNM=3(28)+6=90^\circ$.

The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}y&=360^\circ-120^\circ-90^\circ-90^\circ\\&=60^\circ\end{aligned}$

The interior angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$.

$\begin{aligned}(3z+4)+(5z+16)+(2z+24)+(4z+36)&=360\\14z+80&=360\\14z&=280\\z&=20\end{aligned}$

$\angle DAB=64^\circ$, $\angle ABC=116^\circ$, $\angle BCD=64^\circ$ and $\angle CDA=116^\circ$ (substituting $z=20$).

$\angle DAB+\angle ABC=64^\circ+116^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AD\parallel BC$ (converse of the co-interior angle relationship, transversal $AB$).

$\angle DAB+\angle CDA=64^\circ+116^\circ=180^\circ$, so $AB\parallel DC$ (converse of the co-interior angle relationship, transversal $AD$).

Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

[/tikz]
$ABCD$ is a kite with $AB=AD$ and $CB=CD$.
Find the value of $x$, and hence the value of $y$.
development.solution_text:
$4x-6=2x+30$ (the angles between the unequal sides of a kite are equal)
$2x=36$
$x=18$
$\angle ABC=\angle ADC=4(18)-6=66^{\circ}$
$y=360^{\circ}-88^{\circ}-66^{\circ}-66^{\circ}$
$=140^{\circ}$ (angle sum of a quadrilateral)

$a^{\circ}$, $b^{\circ}$ and $c^{\circ}$ are the reflex angles at the three vertices of the triangle.
Find the value of $a+b+c$, explaining your reasoning.
mastery.solution_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]\coordinate (A) at (-2.2,-1.45);\coordinate (B) at (2.2,-1.45);\coordinate (C) at (0.3,1.45);\draw (A)--(B)--(C)--(A);\draw (-1.841,-1.033) arc[start angle=49.236,end angle=360,radius=0.55];\node at (-3.155,-1.887) {$c^{\circ}$};\draw (1.65,-1.45) arc[start angle=180,end angle=483.232,radius=0.55];\node at (3.124,-1.949) {$a^{\circ}$};\draw (0.601,0.99) arc[start angle=303.232,end angle=589.236,radius=0.55];\node at (0.369,2.498) {$b^{\circ}$};\pic[draw,"$z^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.55cm,angle eccentricity=1.9] {angle=B--A--C};\pic[draw,"$x^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.55cm,angle eccentricity=1.9] {angle=C--B--A};\pic[draw,"$y^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.55cm,angle eccentricity=1.9] {angle=A--C--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Let the interior angles of the triangle be $x^{\circ}$, $y^{\circ}$ and $z^{\circ}$.
$a+x=360$, $b+y=360$ and $c+z=360$ (angles at a point)
$a+b+c+x+y+z=1080$
$x+y+z=180$ (angle sum of a triangle)
$a+b+c=1080-180$
$=900$

[/tikz]
$ACD$ is a straight line, $AB=AC$ and $CB=CD$.
Prove that $x+4y=180$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\angle CBD=y$ (base angles of the isosceles $\triangle BCD$, since $CB=CD$)
$\angle BCD=180-2y$ (angle sum of $\triangle BCD$)
$\angle BCA=180-(180-2y)=2y$ (angles on the straight line $ACD$)
$\angle ABC=2y$ (base angles of the isosceles $\triangle ABC$, since $AB=AC$)
$x+2y+2y=180$ (angle sum of $\triangle ABC$)
$x+4y=180$

$(2x+16)+(7x+29)+(4x-14)+(9x-1)=360$
$22x+30=360$
$22x=330$
$x=15$ (angle sum of a quadrilateral)
$\angle DAB=2(15)+16=46^{\circ}$ and $\angle BCD=4(15)-14=46^{\circ}$, so one pair of opposite angles is equal
$\angle ABC=7(15)+29=134^{\circ}$ and $\angle CDA=9(15)-1=134^{\circ}$, so the other pair of opposite angles is equal
Both pairs of opposite angles are equal, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.

Prove that $a+b=60$.

\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=1]\tikzset{tk/.style={postaction={decorate,decoration={markings,mark=at position 0.5 with {\draw (0pt,-4pt)--(0pt,4pt);}}}},tkk/.style={postaction={decorate,decoration={markings,mark=at position 0.5 with {\draw (-2.5pt,-4pt)--(-2.5pt,4pt);\draw (2.5pt,-4pt)--(2.5pt,4pt);}}}}}\coordinate (A) at (-1.419,1.494);\coordinate (B) at (-1.157,-1.494);\coordinate (C) at (1.3,0.226);\coordinate (TL) at (-2.1,1.494);\coordinate (TR) at (2.1,1.494);\coordinate (BL) at (-2.1,-1.494);\coordinate (BR) at (2.1,-1.494);\coordinate (L) at (-2.1,0.226);\coordinate (Rt) at (2.1,0.226);\draw (TL)--(A);\draw (A)--(TR);\draw (TR)--(BR);\draw (BR)--(B);\draw (B)--(BL);\draw (BL)--(TL);\draw[tk] (A)--(B);\draw[tk] (B)--(C);\draw[tk] (C)--(A);\node[above] at (A) {$A$};\node[below] at (B) {$B$};\node[right] at (C) {$C$};\draw[dashed] (L)--(C);\draw[dashed] (C)--(Rt);\draw[->] (-0.53,1.494)--(0.11,1.494);\draw[->] (-0.53,-1.494)--(0.11,-1.494);\draw[->] (-0.53,0.226)--(0.11,0.226);\pic[draw,"$a^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.7] {angle=C--A--TR};\pic[draw,"$b^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.7cm,angle eccentricity=1.7] {angle=BR--B--C};\pic[draw,"$a^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.95cm,angle eccentricity=1.55] {angle=A--C--L};\pic[draw,"$b^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.95cm,angle eccentricity=1.55] {angle=L--C--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Draw the line through $C$ parallel to the top and bottom sides of the rectangle.
The angle between $CA$ and that line is $a$ (alternate angles, the drawn line is parallel to the top side)
The angle between $CB$ and that line is $b$ (alternate angles, the drawn line is parallel to the bottom side)
The drawn line lies inside $\angle ACB$, so those two angles together make $\angle ACB$.
$a+b=60$ (each angle of an equilateral triangle is $60^{\circ}$)
